title: Wagon band and church fairs: marches, no jazz
summary: At eight or nine he played marches in a small band at church bazaars, which Dance and Edison discuss as Chautauquas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And we played in a band, had a little band around Kentucky that would get on this wagon and we would play for like fairs or something like that that the churches would give a fair. They would call them Chautauquas, you know. That was where they would -- every woman in the church would make a pie, this one would make a cake, this one would make potato salad. Then they would bring it -- a bazaar, like a bazaar, church bazaar, you
know. And they would bring it and sell it to --
Yeah. What is the meaning of Chataqua?
Well, that's an old Indian name for a fair.
Oh, is it? I didn't know that.
Yeah, Chataqua, that's an Indian name for -- I think it is, for a gathering, you know, a lot of people.
What sort of music would you be playing?
Just old band marches, you know. The "Washington Post" march and -- no jazz. No, no, this was just marching. Just the old band, you know.
How old would you be now?
That was when I was about 8 or 9 years old.
